long_biography.plain_text:
Schuerch began in the operating room at South Shore Hospital, where a crude plastic sheet used to move patients suggested a better solution. He cut an early prototype on his mother's living-room floor, tested it at work and learned how to sell it. In 1994, he founded SchureMed while continuing his hospital job, moving into the business full time after its income overtook his wages.

The company grew from that transfer aid into a Massachusetts manufacturer of more than 300 surgical-positioning products and approximately 1,500 components. Its portfolio spans gynecology, urology, orthopaedics and general surgery, with sales to hospitals and surgery centres across the United States and dozens of other countries. Schuerch remains president and chief executive, participates in product design and holds patents for surgical-table supports and clamps. His career combines frontline clinical observation, hands-on invention and long-term operating leadership.
